Count range-test detections per receiver, range-test tag and hour

Source: R/range_test_counts.R
range_test_counts.Rd

Turns the detections of a range test into the counts a range model is fitted to. For every receiver and range-test tag deployed together for a whole bin, the result has one row: the transmissions the tag sent (sent), the detections the receiver logged (heard, zero when it logged none) and the distance between them (distance_m).

Usage

range_test_counts(detections, receivers, tags, bin = "hour")

Arguments

detections

Detections of the range test, one row each: datetime (POSIXct, UTC), receiver_serial and transmitter.

receivers

Receiver deployments of the range test, one row each: receiver_serial, station_id, deploy_datetime, recover_datetime, deploy_lat, deploy_lon and, optionally, deploy_z.

tags

Range-test tags, one row per transmitter: transmitter, deploy_datetime, recover_datetime, deploy_lat, deploy_lon, and either delay or both min_delay and max_delay, in seconds. Other columns, such as tag_model, are carried into the result.

bin

Bin length: "hour", "day" or a number of seconds.

Value

A data frame with one row per receiver, transmitter and bin: datetime (start of the bin, UTC), receiver_serial, station_id, depth_m when receivers has deploy_z, transmitter, the other columns of tags, distance_m, sent and heard.

Details

Every pair, every bin. A bin in which a receiver heard nothing from a tag is kept as a row with heard = 0. These rows matter most at long range, where silence is the common outcome: without them the far end of the curve rests only on the bins that happened to be heard, and the fitted range comes out too long. A receiver and a tag form a pair in a bin when both deployments cover the whole bin.

Transmissions. sent is the bin length over the tag's mean delay, rounded, as in bin_detections(). Where a receiver logged more detections than that in a bin, sent is raised to the count, and a message gives the number of rows raised.

Distance. From the deployment positions of receiver and tag (deploy_lat and deploy_lon, WGS 84), measured on an azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the test and rounded to 0.1 m.

Receiver depth. When receivers has deploy_z, the result carries it as depth_m, the name de_model() passes to a range model.

A deployment with no recover_datetime ends at the last detection in detections. Detections of other transmitters or receivers, and detections in bins that a deployment covers only in part, are not counted; a message gives their number.

See also

de_model(), which wraps the range model fitted to these counts, and vignette("range-model"), which fits one with tag model, receiver depth and wind.

Examples

# The Stoney range test: two lines, at 1 m and 25 m, each of three receivers
# and five range-test tags, for two days. Serial numbers are read as text.
in_file <- function(name) system.file("extdata", name, package = "detfield")
read_utc <- function(name, cols, serial = TRUE) {
  x <- utils::read.csv(in_file(name),
                       colClasses = if (serial) {
                         c(receiver_serial = "character")
                       } else NA)
  for (col in cols) x[[col]] <- as.POSIXct(x[[col]], tz = "UTC")
  x
}
times <- c("deploy_datetime", "recover_datetime")
detections <- read_utc("stoney_range_test_detections.csv", "datetime")
receivers <- read_utc("stoney_range_test_receivers.csv", times)
tags <- read_utc("stoney_range_test_tags.csv", times, serial = FALSE)
# The messages count the detections in part-hours of a deployment, which are
# not counted, and the rows in which a receiver heard more transmissions than
# the mean delay gives, where `sent` is raised.
counts <- range_test_counts(detections, receivers, tags)
#> 121 of 14,281 detections are not counted: other transmitters or
#>   receivers, or bins a deployment covers only in part.
#> 2 of 1,440 rows had more detections than the delay allows
#>   transmissions; `sent` was raised to the count in those rows.
head(counts)
#>     datetime receiver_serial station_id depth_m   transmitter tag_model
#> 1 2024-05-20          480111       RT11       1 A69-9001-9011    V13-1x
#> 2 2024-05-20          480111       RT11       1 A69-9001-9012    V13-1x
#> 3 2024-05-20          480111       RT11       1 A69-9001-9013    V13-1x
#> 4 2024-05-20          480111       RT11       1 A69-9001-9014    V13-1x
#> 5 2024-05-20          480111       RT11       1 A69-9001-9015    V13-1x
#> 6 2024-05-20          480112       RT12       1 A69-9001-9011    V13-1x
#>   distance_m sent heard
#> 1        150   24    17
#> 2        350   24     9
#> 3        650   24     1
#> 4       1100   24     0
#> 5       1600   24     0
#> 6        300   24     6
# Hours in which a receiver heard nothing from a tag stay in, with heard = 0.
c(rows = nrow(counts), heard_nothing = sum(counts$heard == 0))
#>          rows heard_nothing 
#>          1440           400
